$TGT Target lowers prices on nearly 2,000 home, apparel products 
 
Target Corporation is lowering prices on nearly 2,000 home and apparel & accessories items, helping busy families find even more affordable options as holiday shopping gets underway. The latest reductions build on the more than 10,000 prices Target has lowered over the past year, continuing to make it easier for families to afford the things that matter to them. Guests will see price reductions across nearly 2,000 on-trend items and refreshed staples, including: Apparel and shoes: Lower prices across women's, men's, infant and toddler apparel and shoes for the entire family, with select items priced 20% or more lower than last year.  
 
Examples include: Women's long-sleeve tees are now $12, down from $15; The average price of women's shoes is $35, down from $40 last year - with nearly 70% of new items priced below last year's styles; The average price of kids' rain and winter boots is down approximately 15% from last year. Home: A fully refreshed bedding assortment, with prices 15% lower, on average, including: Threshold queen comforters are now $69, down from $89; Room Essentials queen comforters are now $40, down from $50; Threshold performance queen sheets are now $50, down from $55.

Adobe Analytics: Projected $275.1B in US online sales b/n Nov. 1 & Dec. 31, up + 6.7% y/y

Adobe expects Cyber Monday to remain the biggest online shopping day of the season, forecasting $15.1B in a single day of sales, or up +6.2% y/y. 

Adobe projects Black Friday sales will grow at a stronger clip, up +9.2% to $12.9B, due in part to having the biggest discounts on categories like TVs, apparel & appliances.

Adobe said consumers continue to shop for the holidays earlier, w/ $AMZN Prime Day sales event in Oct driving further discounts across US retailers well ahead of Nov. Adobe expects online spending to hit $95.8B in October, up +8% y/y

Adobe also expects consumers to stock up on essentials during holiday deals, projecting online sales of personal hygiene products will more than double-& clothing basics will more than triple-during Cyber Week.

Adobe said its f/casts are based on more than 1T visits to US retail sites, 100M SKUs & 18 product categories

$TGT 
 
One of the quieter retail turnarounds this year: Target is up 61% year to date, and the traffic data underneath is why it looks real. 
 
Comps rose 3.8% last quarter after falling 1.9% the year before. Traffic did the work, up 3.6% while average ticket barely moved. People are coming back, not just spending more per trip. 
 
The headline EPS was flattered by a 994M tariff refund. The cleaner read: ex-refund EPS still grew 20% and beat consensus, and management raised the full-year sales guide to around 5%. 
 
Sept 23 brought the dividend declaration: 1.16 per share payable Dec 1. Per the company's own release, it is the 237th consecutive dividend since 1967.
